nodes.name: Variegated fig
nodes.desc: A fig tree of tropical forest whose fruit is eaten by monkeys, bats and fruit-eating birds, and was recorded in the park area.

nodes.name: Antidesma
nodes.desc: A forest tree recorded near the park whose small fruits are eaten by macaques, according to GloBI records.

nodes.name: Timor murainagrass
nodes.desc: A grass recorded in the park area. Grasses of this kind grow in open and floodplain ground and feed grazers such as deer.

nodes.name: Timor deer
nodes.desc: Native deer eating grass, leaves and fallen fruit. It is listed as vulnerable, and dry-season water shortages have killed deer on Jaco Island.

nodes.name: Crab-eating macaque
nodes.desc: An omnivorous monkey recorded in the park area. It eats fruit such as figs and Antidesma, and also insects.

nodes.name: Black-backed fruit dove
nodes.desc: A very commonly recorded forest bird of the area that feeds mainly on fruit, including figs, and spreads seeds.

nodes.name: Pink-headed imperial pigeon
nodes.desc: A large fruit pigeon of Lesser Sunda forests, rated near threatened, and listed among the park's notable birds.

nodes.name: Northern blossom bat
nodes.desc: A small fruit and nectar bat. GloBI records show it eating fig fruit, and it helps pollinate and spread forest plants.

nodes.name: Northern common cuscus
nodes.desc: A tree-living marsupial that eats leaves and fruit. It was brought to Timor about 9,000 years ago and is hunted by local people.

nodes.name: Small brown crow
nodes.desc: A butterfly of the crow group, whose caterpillars feed on forest plants such as figs, and adults take nectar.

nodes.name: Polynesian rat
nodes.desc: A small introduced rodent that eats seeds, fruit and insects. It is food for snakes and other predators.

nodes.name: Green marsh hawk
nodes.desc: A common dragonfly of wetlands that hunts other flying insects, including smaller dragonflies, per GloBI.

nodes.name: Rainbow bee-eater
nodes.desc: A bird that catches flying insects in the air, including dragonflies, and was recorded often around the park.

nodes.name: Four-lined tree frog
nodes.desc: A tree frog that eats insects. It is prey for snakes such as the white-lipped island pitviper, according to GloBI.

nodes.name: White-lipped island pitviper
nodes.desc: A venomous tree snake and the most recorded reptile near the park. GloBI records show it eating tree frogs.

nodes.name: Timor python
nodes.desc: A python of the Lesser Sunda islands that preys on rodents and birds. It is a top land predator in this web.

nodes.name: Saltwater crocodile
nodes.desc: An opportunistic top predator of coasts and rivers that takes deer and many other animals. It is considered holy on Timor.

nodes.name: Tropical sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong year-round sun lets the forest and grassland plants grow all year when water is available.

nodes.name: Monsoon rains
nodes.desc: Rain comes mostly in a wet season. When the rains fail, as in late 2019, water points dry up and deer suffer.

nodes.name: Lake Ira Lalaro wetland
nodes.desc: The park's large freshwater lake and flood plain; its marshy margins grow grasses and are grazed by village livestock.

nodes.name: Forest soil
nodes.desc: Soil on limestone terraces and lowland ground that holds the nutrients and water plants draw on.

nodes.name: Fungi and soil life
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, fruit and dead animals and return nutrients to the soil.
